strictMethods: Water sautéing — heat the dry pan first, add vegetables, then a tablespoon of water only when they stick; repeat. The sticking is where the flavour comes from.
Vegetable-broth sautéing — the same, with more taste in the liquid.
Dry-searing mushrooms — no liquid at all until they release their own; do not crowd the pan.
Onions without oil — low and slow in a heavy pan, deglazing with a spoon of water each time they catch; 25 minutes gets real depth.
Steaming — for greens and tender vegetables you will dress afterwards with lemon.
Boiling and simmering — soups and stews carry the fast; make them thick.
Baking on parchment at 220°C / 425°F — potatoes, chickpeas and root vegetables crisp without a drop of oil.
Pressure cooking — dried beans without soaking, dal in six minutes.
Slow cooking — assemble in the morning, come home to supper.
Season late and season hard — vinegar, lemon, mustard, herbs and salt do the work fat usually does.
strictNote: Added oil and naturally occurring fat are different things. Olive oil poured into a pan is added oil, and the GOARCH legend sets it aside on strict days. The fat inside a walnut, an olive on the branch, an avocado, or a spoonful of tahini is part of a whole food — households, jurisdictions and spiritual fathers differ on how to treat those, and this app does not rule on it. Ask your priest. The same goes for shellfish and for wine substitutes: practice varies, and the table below never overrides your parish.
